Q1025448: County-level city in southern Hunan under Hengyang.
Hometown of Cai Lun, the Han-dynasty official credited with inventing paper.
A tomb attributed to the Tang poet Du Fu, who died in this region, is in the city.
Q659887: Town in central Kerala, called the 'City of Letters'.
Birthplace of major Malayalam newspapers like Malayala Manorama and Deepika.
The first town in India to reach 100% literacy (1989).
A centre of rubber plantations and Syrian Christian churches.
Q362865: City in western Jiangxi bordering Hunan.
The 1922 Anyuan coal miners' strike, led by Liu Shaoqi and Li Lisan, was an early Communist labour success.
Part of the 1927 Autumn Harvest Uprising led by Mao.
Known for fireworks and Wugong Mountain.
Q765487: Town in Fars province, about 80 km southeast of Shiraz.
Its Sasanian palace (5th century) is part of a World Heritage Site.
Known for its yoghurt and olive and pistachio farming.
Q25247670: Town and block in Siwan district, Bihar.
Part of the densely populated Bhojpuri-speaking plain of western Bihar.
Hit by floods of the Daha River in 2001.
Q367354: Coastal town in Kannur district, Kerala; called Tellicherry by the British.
Known as the land of the 'three Cs': cricket, cake and circus — Kerala's first cricket match and first bakery cake are traced here.
The British East India Company built a fort here in 1708.
Famous for Thalassery biryani and Tellicherry pepper.
Q47492: The largest city of the Gaza Strip, on the Mediterranean.
Inhabited for over 3,000 years; one of the five Philistine cities.
Under Israeli blockade since 2007 and largely destroyed in the war that began in 2023.
Ash Shati (Beach) refugee camp lies on its coast.
Q425996: Industrial city in Sichuan, north of Chengdu.
The Sanxingdui site in Guanghan, with mysterious bronze masks and statues over 3,000 years old, is here.
A centre of heavy machinery making, such as Dongfang Electric turbines.
Badly hit by the 2008 Sichuan earthquake.
Q34863: Founded in a single day in the Land Run of 22 April 1889, when settlers raced to claim land.
Site of the 1995 Oklahoma City bombing, the deadliest domestic terror attack in US history.
Known for cowboy culture and oil wells on the Capitol grounds.
Q321079: Capital of Plateau State in central Nigeria, at about 1,200 m.
Grew with tin mining under British rule.
Has a cooler climate than most of Nigeria; the Jos Museum and wildlife park are known.
Has suffered from ethnic and religious violence.
Q131323: Libya's third city, on the Mediterranean east of Tripoli.
Libya's commercial capital with an important port and steel works.
Withstood a long siege by Gaddafi's forces in the 2011 civil war.
Q18575: Arizona's second city, in the Sonoran Desert surrounded by mountains.
Home of the University of Arizona and Saguaro National Park with giant cacti.
Has a famous 'aircraft boneyard' at Davis–Monthan Air Force Base.
A UNESCO City of Gastronomy, the first in the US.
Q500366: Second city of Oyo State in southwestern Nigeria.
Founded in the mid-17th century; seat of the Soun of Ogbomosho.
Home of Ladoke Akintola University of Technology.
Many emigrants from Ogbomosho live elsewhere in Nigeria and abroad.
Q33486: Called the 'Insurance Capital of the World': Aetna, The Hartford and Travelers are based here.
Mark Twain wrote Tom Sawyer and Huckleberry Finn while living here.
Its Hartford Courant is the oldest continuously published US newspaper.
Q1198335: District of Jinan in Shandong, formerly the separate city of Laiwu.
Merged into Jinan in 2019; known for Laiwu black pigs and ginger.
Q319804: Resort city at the southern tip of Hainan, China's tropical island.
Called the 'Hawaii of China' for its beaches like Yalong Bay.
The Guanyin of the South Sea statue (108 m) stands in the sea at Nanshan.
Hosted Miss World several times; has a big duty-free mall.
Q795595: Provincial capital in southern Thailand, on Songkhla Lake near Malaysia.
Forms a metro area with Hat Yai, the region's commercial centre.
Known for Samila Beach and its golden mermaid statue.
An old port with Chinese and Malay influences.
Q34404: City in Louisiana on the Mississippi near the Gulf of Mexico; nicknamed 'The Big Easy'.
Founded by the French in 1718; its French Quarter keeps Creole architecture.
Birthplace of jazz (Louis Armstrong) and famous for Mardi Gras and Creole and Cajun food.
Devastated by Hurricane Katrina in 2005 when the levees failed.
Q59107: City in northern Guangdong, bordering Hunan and Jiangxi.
The Nanhua Temple holds the mummified body of Huineng, the Sixth Patriarch of Zen Buddhism.
Mount Danxia, which gave its name to red-sandstone 'Danxia' landforms, is a World Heritage Site.
Q914: City on the Volga in southern Russia; called Tsaritsyn until 1925 and Stalingrad from 1925 to 1961.
The Battle of Stalingrad (1942–43) was a turning point of WWII and one of the bloodiest battles in history.
The Motherland Calls statue on Mamayev Kurgan is one of the tallest statues in the world.
Stretches about 80 km along the Volga.
Q170967: Gateway to Pamukkale's white travertine terraces and the ruins of Hierapolis (World Heritage Site).
A big centre of cotton textiles, especially towels.
Famous for the Denizli rooster, a long-crowing breed.
Q81882: Port city on São Vicente island in São Paulo state.
Its port is the busiest in Latin America and once set world coffee prices (Coffee Museum).
Home of Santos FC, where Pelé played; Pelé's memorial and tomb are here.
Has the world's longest beachfront garden (Guinness).
Q768864: City just north of Bangkok, Thailand's second-largest city municipality.
Grew as a suburb of Bangkok along the Chao Phraya River.
Known for its durian orchards and Ko Kret island with Mon pottery villages.
Q34370: Second city of the Netherlands at the mouth of the Rhine and Meuse; Europe's largest seaport.
Its centre was destroyed by German bombing in 1940 and rebuilt with modern architecture.
Famous for the cube houses, the Erasmus Bridge and the Markthal.
The scholar Erasmus was born here.
Q1005770: Coastal municipality of Luanda Province, a fast-growing suburb northeast of Luanda.
An industrial centre with Angola's landing station for the SAT-3 undersea cable.
Q269960: Egypt's fourth-largest city, on the northern edge of Cairo in Qalyubiyya.
One of Egypt's main industrial areas (textiles, chemicals).
The name means 'hamlet of the tent'.
Q28979: Coal-mining city in southeastern Heilongjiang, near the Russian border.
Near Lake Khanka (Xingkai), shared with Russia.
A crater on the asteroid 253 Mathilde is named after it.
Q31356: The main city of the Swat Valley in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, Pakistan.
Hometown of Malala Yousafzai, the youngest Nobel Peace Prize laureate.
The Swat Valley was a centre of Gandhara Buddhism; nicknamed the 'Switzerland of Pakistan'.
Q33986: Port city on Chile's Pacific coast and seat of the National Congress.
Its colourful hillside neighbourhoods, linked by funiculars (ascensores), are a World Heritage Site.
Was the main port of the Pacific before the Panama Canal opened in 1914.
The poet Pablo Neruda had a house here (La Sebastiana).
Q199909: Holy city of Shia Islam in central Iraq.
Site of the Battle of Karbala (680), where Husayn, grandson of the Prophet, was killed.
His shrine draws millions of pilgrims, especially during the Arbaeen walk, one of the largest gatherings in the world.
Q1629: City at the southwestern tip of Mindanao, Philippines.
Called 'Asia's Latin City': many people speak Chavacano, a Spanish-based creole.
Fort Pilar was built by the Spanish in 1635.
Q838785: City in Riverside County, California, part of the Temecula–Murrieta area.
Known for the Temecula Valley wine country and its Old Town.
Has the Pechanga Resort Casino of the Pechanga Band of Luiseño Indians nearby.
Q58710: City in Hebei between Beijing and Tianjin.
Includes Yanjiao and Sanhe, commuter towns for Beijing.
Q271771: Capital of Gharbia Governorate in the Nile Delta.
Its mosque of the Sufi saint Ahmad al-Badawi draws huge crowds to his yearly festival (mawlid).
Known for sweets and roasted chickpeas; home of Tanta University.
Q1479: City on the Garonne in southwestern France, capital of Nouvelle-Aquitaine.
World capital of wine: the Bordeaux region includes Médoc and Saint-Émilion.
Its 18th-century 'Port of the Moon' centre is a World Heritage Site.
Has the Water Mirror in front of the Place de la Bourse and the Cité du Vin museum.
Q3646: Southern Russia's largest city, on the Kuban River.
Founded in 1793 as Yekaterinodar, a fortress of the Black Sea Cossacks.
Centre of Russia's richest farming region; home of FC Krasnodar.
Gateway to the Black Sea coast resorts like Sochi.
Q708605: Coastal new area of Tianjin on the Bohai Sea.
A major port and free-trade zone and site of the Tianjin Eco-City.
Site of the 2015 Tianjin explosions at a chemical warehouse that killed 173 people.
The Binhai Library is famous for its eye-shaped atrium.
Q170525: City on Morocco's Atlantic coast at the foot of the Atlas, capital of the Souss-Massa region.
Destroyed by the 1960 earthquake and rebuilt as a modern beach resort.
Its Kasbah on the hill has the slogan 'God, Country, King' in giant letters.
Considered a capital of Amazigh (Berber) culture and of argan oil.
Q200252: Capital of Michoacán in central Mexico; called Valladolid until 1828.
Renamed after José María Morelos, hero of independence, who was born here.
Its colonial centre built of pink stone is a World Heritage Site; has a long colonial aqueduct.
Gateway to the monarch butterfly reserves.
Q1874: Ukraine's main port on the Black Sea, founded by Catherine the Great in 1794.
Famous for the Potemkin Stairs, shown in Eisenstein's 1925 film 'Battleship Potemkin'.
A multicultural city known for its humour and its Opera Theatre; its centre became a World Heritage Site in 2023.
Has a huge maze of catacombs under the city.
Q217646: City in southeastern Heilongjiang on the Mudan River.
Near Jingpo Lake, a volcanic lake with the Diaoshuilou waterfall.
A transport hub for trade with Russia (Suifenhe).
Q58724: Famous for Hengshui High School, known for its extremely strict study regime.
Known for Hengshui Laobaigan liquor and the Hengshui Lake wetland.
Hometown of the Han-dynasty Confucian philosopher Dong Zhongshu.
Q159273: Peru's second city, in a valley below the El Misti volcano.
Called the 'White City' for its buildings of white volcanic stone (sillar); its centre is a World Heritage Site.
Home of the Santa Catalina Monastery, a city within the city.
The 'Juanita' Inca ice mummy is kept here; gateway to the Colca Canyon.
Q322155: City in northwestern Bangladesh on the Padma River, near the Indian border.
Famous for Rajshahi silk and mangoes.
Called the 'City of Education'; home of the Varendra Research Museum, Bangladesh's oldest museum.
Known as one of the cleanest and greenest cities in Bangladesh.
Q16562: City in West Texas on the Rio Grande, across from Ciudad Juárez, Mexico.
Named after the mountain pass 'El Paso del Norte'.
Home of Fort Bliss, one of the largest US Army bases.
Mostly Hispanic and known for Tex-Mex food.
Q362959: Known as a steel city (Xinyu Steel) and a centre of solar-panel making (LDK).
The Fairy Lake (Xiannu Lake) is linked to the legend of the Seven Fairies.
Q73156: City in southern Shanxi on the Fen River, called Pingyang in antiquity.
Traditionally the capital of the legendary Emperor Yao.
Was once called one of the world's most polluted cities because of coal mining.
The Hukou Waterfall on the Yellow River is in the prefecture.
Q1525057: City in West Bengal on the Mahananda River, also called English Bazar.
Famous for mangoes (e.g. Fazli) and silk.
Near the ruins of Gauda and Pandua, old capitals of medieval Bengal.
Q506250: The City of Stockholm, the largest municipality of Sweden and the Nordic countries.
Spread across 14 islands where Lake Mälaren meets the Baltic Sea.
The Nobel Prizes (except Peace) are awarded here; known for Gamla stan and the Vasa Museum.
Q71468: City in central Hubei on the Jianghan Plain, west of Wuhan.
Hometown of Lu Yu, author of 'The Classic of Tea', honoured as the 'Sage of Tea'.
Has many emigrants and is known as a 'hometown of overseas Chinese'.
Q604609: County-level city in Hunan under Zhuzhou.
Famous for underglaze porcelain; Mao Zedong's personal tableware came from Liling.
One of the birthplaces of fireworks, with Liuyang.
Q639421: Capital of the Union Territory of Puducherry on the Bay of Bengal.
The main town of French India until 1954; its French Quarter has yellow villas and French street names.
Home of the Sri Aurobindo Ashram; the experimental town Auroville is nearby.
Q360069: City in northern Anhui on the Huai River; the name means 'clam wharf'.
A railway junction on the Beijing–Shanghai line; near Fengyang, hometown of the first Ming emperor.
Q14126: Capital of West Nusa Tenggara on the island of Lombok, Indonesia.
Gateway to Mount Rinjani, Lombok's volcano, and the Gili Islands.
Has Hindu Balinese temples like Pura Meru alongside a Muslim Sasak majority; known as an 'island of a thousand mosques'.
Q169134: Capital of Nara Prefecture; Japan's capital from 710 to 784.
Tōdai-ji temple houses a giant bronze Buddha in one of the largest wooden buildings in the world.
About 1,000 sacred deer roam freely in Nara Park and bow for crackers.
Its old temples and shrines are a World Heritage Site.
Q127041: Port city on Karnataka's west coast between the Arabian Sea and the Western Ghats.
An ancient spice and coffee port; New Mangalore Port is a major Indian port.
Known for its Tulu culture, Yakshagana theatre and seafood.
Q104682488: The urban community of Dnipro, a major city in central-eastern Ukraine on the Dnieper River.
A Soviet centre of the rocket and space industry (Yuzhmash), long closed to foreigners.
Has one of the longest riverside promenades in Europe.
Q59184: City in eastern Guangdong, the 'world capital of the Hakka people'.
Ancestral home of many overseas Hakka Chinese.
Called the 'hometown of football' in China; known for Hakka round houses (weilongwu).
Q507080: Planned city in Venezuela where the Caroní River meets the Orinoco.
Founded in 1961 by merging old San Félix with the new steel town Puerto Ordaz.
Centre of Venezuela's heavy industry: steel, aluminium and the Guri hydroelectric dam.
Has waterfalls inside the city parks (Cachamay and La Llovizna).
Q251329: Second city of Bihar, sacred to Hindus, Buddhists and Jains.
Hindus come to perform pinda daan rites for their ancestors at the Vishnupad Temple.
Bodh Gaya, where the Buddha attained enlightenment under the Bodhi tree, is about 15 km away (World Heritage Site).
